children: By Rajendra Jadhav and Ashitha Shivaprasad

Gold discounts in India plunged this week, falling to their deepest level in three months, as demand fell sharply amid market speculation that the government could consider rolling back a recent hike in import duties.

In May, India raised import duties on gold and silver to 15% from 6%. Traders have speculated that smuggling has increased since the duty hike and that the government could restore the previous duty structure to curb it.

"Rumours about a duty cut made buyers hold off on purchases. Demand suddenly dropped," said Chanda Venkatesh, managing director at CapsGold, a bullion merchant based in the southern city of Hyderabad.
Dealers quoted a discount (XAU-IN-PREM) of up to $135 an ounce over official domestic prices, inclusive of 15% import and 3% sales levies, compared to last week’s $65 discount.
Domestic gold prices (MAUc1) were trading around 158,000 rupees ($1,653.41) per 10 grams on Friday after scaling to their highest level since early March on Monday.

Jewellers need to replenish stocks ahead of the upcoming festival season, but they have stayed on the sidelines, hoping for a cut in import duties, a Mumbai-based bullion dealer with a private bank said.
In China, (XAU-CN-PREM), bullion traded at discounts of $2 to $5 an ounce to the global benchmark spot price, compared with prices on par with the benchmark to a $6 premium last week.

"There was good buying interest when gold prices were lower than current levels. But with an uptick in prices some buyers have stepped back, and others have taken profits," said Peter Fung, head of dealing at Wing Fung Precious Metals.
International spot gold prices slipped on Friday but gained more than 5% last week.
In Singapore (XAU-SG-PREM), gold was sold between a $1 discount and a premium of up to $2.50 this week, while in Hong Kong (XAU-HK-PREM) it traded from a $1 discount to a $1.5 premium.

"We saw some wholesalers come in to short-cover. Meanwhile, wealthier clients were buying, as they view gold as a safe investment because the world is not in a good place right now," said Brian Lan, managing director at GoldSilver Central.
In Japan , gold was sold between a $0.50 discount and a $ 1 premium.
